vulnerable_statements.reason: uoffsets is an attacker-controlled pointer taken from the bpf_attr, and access_ok() is never called on it. __get_user() skips the address-range check, so a kernel address can be passed in and kernel memory is read as if it were user memory.
Same problem: uref_ctr_offsets comes from the user and is read with __get_user() without access_ok(), so it can point into kernel memory.
Same problem: ucookies comes from the user and is read with __get_user() without access_ok(), so it can point into kernel memory.

suggested_fix: Use get_user() instead of __get_user() for all three user arrays, because get_user() checks the address range itself. Another option is to call access_ok() on uoffsets, uref_ctr_offsets and ucookies for cnt elements before the loop, or to copy each whole array with copy_from_user(). This is what the upstream fix did: it switched these reads to get_user().
